documents.title: Your Classroom Faculty Guide to AI
documents.summary: A teaching-center page advising Rush faculty on AI. It tells them to set their own expectations, require an AI Use Disclosure and citations, redesign assessments, and not rely on detectors, and it welcomes faculty use of AI. It sets no student-wide rule.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no ban or permission itself; it says faculty should 'Set clear expectations for your students on whether and how they can use AI sources' and may 'allow it only for certain purposes', which hands the decision to instructors, so delegates.

units.why: Advises educators to 'start with a clear pedagogical purpose' when implementing AI; guidance to instructors on course design that fits no existing type (not a stance, not an AI-statement rule).
units.resolution_why: Coder A: UNCOVERED (guidance to start with a clear pedagogical purpose, no type fits); coder B: P35 with a fit note ('Advice to design AI activities with a learning purpose; not a grading or assignment redesign rule as such'). The source says 'it is crucial to start with a clear pedagogical purpose. Identifying specific learning objectives or challenges that can be addressed through AI technology...'. P35 is about redesigning assignments and grading around AI; this passage is about choosing a purpose before adopting AI in a course, which P35 does not say, and B's own fit note concedes this. Final: UNCOVERED, before-course, should, encourage.

notes: Single included document (CTEI faculty guide); advisory prose for faculty, no student-facing binding policy and no computing unit. Health-sciences university. Images and the Six Best Practices graphic are not in the saved text. Recurring UNCOVERED themes: limits of enforcement (AI use cannot be eliminated; hard to know how much students use AI), and instructor guidance on purpose-driven adoption.
